findings.title: Answer keys are disclosed on every submission, enabling retry farming
findings.evidence: app/api/guided-path/[trackId]/route.ts:204-218 returns correctIndex and explanation for every question, including validateOnly and failed submissions.
findings.impact: A learner can submit arbitrary integers, receive every key, and resubmit to pass. Quizzes that gate progression or paid content are effectively open-book.
findings.requiredChange: Choose a graded, formative, or hybrid policy. Never return correctIndex in a graded flow; add server-side attempts and rate limiting; do not let validateOnly act as a free key oracle.
findings.exitTest: Failed/validateOnly responses contain no key material; repeated immediate submissions are blocked or served a different variant; attempts are recorded.

findings.title: No quiz attempt, score, or version persistence; prior passes survive harder quizzes
findings.evidence: prisma/schema.prisma has no quiz tables; LearningEvent records quiz_failed metadata but not a durable attempt. Completion is a UserProgress row keyed q:<stage>; path-compat remaps positions but does not invalidate passes.
findings.impact: A learner who passed the old 3-question quiz keeps completion after a 5-question quiz is imported. There is no audit trail, retry control, or version invalidation.
findings.requiredChange: Persist attempts with pathVersion and quizVersion; require a current-version pass or an explicit grandfather policy; never silently treat legacy completion as current.
findings.exitTest: A new quiz version forces a new attempt or an explicit legacy flag; attempts are queryable; a path-version bump preserves position without marking the new quiz complete.

findings.title: Bundle quiz fields are silently discarded by the runtime
findings.evidence: QuizQuestion supports only question/options/correctIndex/explanation plus optional teaching metadata; the grader counts correct answers and ignores points, critical, correctAnswer, rationales, and distractor analysis.
findings.impact: Critical gates and 20-point weights are illusory; the 100-point score is only a percentage of correct count; rich feedback never reaches learners.
findings.requiredChange: Either normalize to the four-field contract at import and report dropped fields, or extend the type and grader with weighted/critical support. Do not import extra fields silently.
findings.exitTest: Import report lists every dropped field; critical/weighted behavior matches the chosen policy; score semantics are asserted.

findings.title: Project artifact kinds and rubrics do not match the evaluator
findings.evidence: Runtime supports 14 ArtifactKind values; the package uses at least 29 more. parseArtifacts casts arbitrary strings. The evaluator derives rubrics from acceptanceCriteria, not the package effectiveRubric.
findings.impact: Learners are asked for different evidence than the package specifies; unknown kinds can reach the pipeline; package weights and mandatory flags never reach the evaluator. cyber and qa both map to security, whose base contract requires github_repo; manual report deliverables need explicit overrides.
findings.requiredChange: Add strict kind validation with 422, publish an explicit kind mapping, carry artifact labels, and decide per project whether package rubrics are imported or replaced by runtime derivation.
findings.exitTest: All 125 projects resolve; required kinds are in the enum; unknown kinds return 422; missing required evidence cannot pass.

findings.title: All AI tracks default to the software discipline
findings.evidence: disciplineForTrack has no ai-* entries and falls back to software; the legacy ai track is explicitly in SOFTWARE_TRACKS.
findings.impact: AI Foundations, Work, Research, Content, YouTube, Automation, Engineering, and Design inherit the software default (public inspectable source, README, source inspection), conflicting with their non-code evidence formats.
findings.requiredChange: Add explicit AI discipline routing or per-project overrides; resolve all 125 projects to a discipline and artifact set; test the 10 capstones.
findings.exitTest: No AI project requires github_repo unless its brief asks for code; each capstone has discipline-appropriate artifacts.

findings.title: The external-resource gate is unmet and the runtime would overstate it
findings.evidence: 143 provisional primaries, 43 blocked stages, 0 current live reverifications, 0 playback checks. isResourceVerified checks level >= 3 plus 600+ characters of content evidence but does not check access at all, so a paid resource can pass.
findings.impact: Wiring these as required would create false verified claims, dead/paid links, and the appearance that blocked stages are solved.
findings.requiredChange: Do not import any package resource as a required primary. Stage them as archive evidence with role optional; promote only after a fresh check; keep blocked stages optional-only.
findings.exitTest: No required primary has only archive evidence; all 43 blocked stages have no required external primary; archive vs current is distinguishable.

findings.title: authoredInstruction is an outline, not a complete in-product lesson
findings.evidence: Stage specs contain outlines/worked examples, not full lesson prose with explanations and practice. Blocked stages have no verified external primary.
findings.impact: Demoting the external primary for a blocked stage leaves an outline and a project, not a teachable lesson; claiming otherwise would be inaccurate.
findings.requiredChange: For each of the 43 blocked stages: author and review complete lesson content, keep a verified primary, or mark the stage project-only/supplementary.
findings.exitTest: Each blocked stage has reviewed lesson content or a verified primary; objective coverage is checked; no outline-only stage is presented as complete.

findings.title: Attempt and verification persistence does not exist
findings.evidence: No quiz attempts, quiz versions, resource verification, or normalized project submissions in Prisma; project history is JSON in UserTrackProgress.data.
findings.impact: P0-1 and P0-2 cannot be fixed reliably; resource promotion cannot be audited; rubric invalidation and evidence reuse are hard to query.
findings.requiredChange: Add additive QuizAttempt, StageQuizVersion, ResourceVerificationRecord tables; optionally normalize ProjectSubmission later. Proposal only; no migration in this phase.
findings.exitTest: Migration is additive, backfills no fabricated attempts, preserves progress, and is gated by a flag with rollback.

findings.title: Static bundle rubric version conflicts with runtime-derived version
findings.evidence: All package mastery records use tsh-stage-rubric-v1; runtime computes a hash from criteria via computeRubricVersion and uses it in the evidence fingerprint.
findings.impact: Importing the static version can reuse passes across different criteria; using the runtime version invalidates correctly but diverges from package provenance.
findings.requiredChange: Derive the runtime version from criteria and store the package version as provenance only; test that criteria changes invalidate reuse.
findings.exitTest: Any criteria change produces a new version and blocks reuse; provenance still records the package version.

findings.title: Mandatory flags contradict the progression gate
findings.evidence: Many package rubric items are mandatory:false while progressionGate.criticalCriteriaMustPass is true; runtime adds discipline mandatory criteria.
findings.impact: A learner can meet the weighted threshold while failing a criterion the package calls critical, or face stricter runtime criteria than intended.
findings.requiredChange: Reconcile each project: map criteria to runtime mandatory flags or correct the gate text. Do not ship contradictory specs.
findings.exitTest: Every project has an explicit mandatory set; failing a mandatory criterion blocks progression.

findings.title: AI quiz repetition and cross-domain contamination
findings.evidence: lib/ai-assessment-bank.ts reuses generic supplemental questions; six QUIZ-CROSS leakage issues (crypto-6, fullstack-2/3/4, mobile-4, qa-4); AI-QUIZ-REPEATS reports 70/76 AI stages had only one topic-specific old question and ai-content:6 had zero, though the package replaces them with five stage-scoped items pending SME review.
findings.impact: Learners see repeated questions, wrong-domain items, and weak validity.
findings.requiredChange: Review all 930 for stage specificity and objective match; replace generic bank reuse; close the six leakage issues before those tracks ship.
findings.exitTest: No duplicate stems across stages; each question maps to the stage objective; leakage issues closed.

findings.title: QA audit is internally stale
findings.evidence: QUIZ-QA-001 claims 67 duplicate stem groups while the QA summary reports zero; the repair log and specificity audit disagree.
findings.impact: Reviewers cannot trust duplicate counts; repair may be repeated or skipped.
findings.requiredChange: Recompute duplicates from the current 930-row bank, record the algorithm and output hash, and retire the stale row.
findings.exitTest: One reproducible duplicate report, referenced by the package.

findings.title: Video evidence is not playback-verified
findings.evidence: VIDEO-RUNTIME reports 60 video rows with no runtime/segment evidence; none is L4 playback-verified; the package says not to expose 30-90 minute estimates as verified.
findings.impact: Required video portions cannot be timed or checked; learners may be sent to the wrong segment.
findings.requiredChange: Keep video optional until playback and timestamps are captured; prefer text/interactive resources for required learning.
findings.exitTest: Every required video has playback evidence, start/end timestamps, and a checked segment.

findings.title: Duplicate URLs and cross-stage reuse
findings.evidence: 82 duplicate candidate URLs, 178 duplicate map URL rows, 44 duplicate rows in the repository probe.
findings.impact: The same source may be primary for stages with different objectives; a single failure affects multiple stages.
findings.requiredChange: Dedupe per stage, require exact portion/segment for reuse, and cap shared required primaries.
findings.exitTest: No required primary is reused without an explicit portion and objective justification.

findings.title: Commercial and provider-cost consequences are real
findings.evidence: Project assessment requires track access, consumes assessment credits, and calls the DeepSeek provider; 125 projects increase assessment volume.
findings.impact: Content import can change unit economics and provider load without pricing edits.
findings.requiredChange: Keep commercial gates untouched; model assessment volume; set pilot budgets/quotas; require approval before paid exposure.
findings.exitTest: Pilot stays within a defined assessment budget; no entitlement or price change is bundled with content.

findings.title: Licensing, attribution, and accessibility are not evidenced
findings.evidence: Resource records have publisher/URL/content excerpt but no license/attribution field; no accessibility review is present.
findings.impact: Required third-party use may exceed permitted terms; learners may face inaccessible resources.
findings.requiredChange: Add license/attribution and accessibility fields; treat both as human/legal gates.
findings.exitTest: Every required resource has a recorded license/attribution decision and accessibility note.

findings.title: Stale missing-normalized-brief issues
findings.evidence: The open-issue file has 10 missing_normalized_project_brief rows, one per AI capstone. They describe the package source export, not the current repo: all ten capstones have briefs in lib/ai-project-briefs.ts and definitions in ai-curriculum/ai-projects.
findings.impact: Reviewers may treat the capstones as missing, or import the package draft without comparing it to the existing brief.
findings.requiredChange: Compare each package draft with the existing repo brief and contract, reconcile differences, close the row, and do not report the capstones as missing.
findings.exitTest: Open-issue file has no stale missing-brief rows.

findings.title: The package implementation prompt does not match this repository
findings.evidence: 11_IDE_IMPLEMENTATION_PROMPT.md does not reflect the curriculum/extended/AI module split or the project-verification contract.
findings.impact: Following it literally would create parallel sources of truth.
findings.requiredChange: Replace it with this repo-specific plan before implementation.
findings.exitTest: Implementation prompt names the actual target modules and gates.

finalAnswer: Implementation is safe to start only as a branch-confined, feature-flagged staging and guardrail effort. It is not safe to import the package into learner-facing paths, enable paid access, or claim verification. Fix the P0 runtime contracts, keep 143 provisional resources provisional and all 43 blocked stages optional-only, obtain SME review for the first wave, and promote resources only after fresh live checks.
